FROM REQUEST TO DELIVERY

From your brief.
To your front door.

GLASS QUALITY. CLEAR COSTS.A human-led journey, with the specification, responsibilities and delivery scope agreed before you order.

  1. 01
    YOU → FABINT

    Send your brief

    Tell us your window sizes, glass requirements, quantity, delivery location and target date. A drawing or photo helps.

  2. 02
    FABINT → YOU

    Compare your options

    We aim to return up to three quotes within seven days, showing costs in AUD, glass specifications and anything still to confirm.

  3. 03
    YOUR APPROVAL

    Approve the details

    Choose an option and agree the final specification, price, payment terms, delivery scope and lead time in writing.

  4. 04
    AFTER APPROVAL

    Make and check

    The supplier prepares your order. Quality evidence and any agreed inspection are reviewed before dispatch.

  5. 05
    SUPPLIER → CARRIER

    Arrange shipping

    Imported orders follow the agreed freight and customs arrangements; local orders travel within Australia. Confirm GST, duty and delivery inclusions.

  6. 06
    CARRIER → YOU

    Delivered to your door

    Delivery follows the agreed destination and access arrangements. Check your goods on arrival and report any damage promptly.

GOOD TO KNOW

Typical order journey, subject to agreed supplier terms. Seven days is our quote target—not a delivery promise. Installation and independent inspection are included only when explicitly quoted.

Submitting a request is not placing an order. Our pilot is personally managed; we do not take online payments.

SCROLL TO BRING THE LAYERS TOGETHER ↓

KNOW YOUR GLASS

Different glass.
Different jobs.

Low-E, toughened and double glazing are not competing choices. They describe different parts of a window—and can work together.

01 / COMFORT

Manage heat.

Low-E is a coating; double glazing is a sealed two-pane unit. Both can contribute to thermal comfort, depending on the full window specification.

Low-E & double glazing ↗
02 / SAFETY

Know how it breaks.

Toughened glass breaks into small fragments. Laminated glass uses an interlayer to help hold fragments together. The right choice depends on the application.

Toughened & laminated ↗
03 / LIGHT & PRIVACY

Choose the view.

Clear glass preserves views, tint changes light and glare, and frosted or obscure glass softens visibility. None of these labels alone confirms safety performance.

Clear, tinted & obscure ↗

Seven glass types explained, with typical uses, limitations and manufacturer references.
